hero: In a bright freestanding hemodialysis unit in Pampanga, a Filipino pediatric nephrologist in a white coat kneels at eye level beside a 9-year-old Filipino boy reclining in a dialysis chair with a tunneled chest catheter; his mother sits close holding his hand while a Filipino dialysis nurse checks the machine; adult patients are visible in the background, warm afternoon light, calm and reassuring mood, no text.

figures.teaches: Professional, facility and payer permissions are issued by different authorities and do not substitute for each other.
figures.content: Three columns. Column 1 'Professional': PRC license; specialty certification (PNSP); answers 'Am I trained?'. Column 2 'Facility': privileges from credentials committee; DOH facility license; answers 'May I do this here?'. Column 3 'Payer': PhilHealth accreditation; Z package contracting; answers 'Will it be covered?'. Bottom banner: 'Coverage is not a prescription'. Small crossed-out arrows between columns labeled 'does not replace'.

figures.teaches: A closed-loop call ends with a named owner and a read-back.
figures.content: Six numbered steps left to right: 1 'Identify' (name, age, weight, place); 2 'Situation' (what changed, numbers, time); 3 'Decision' (order said in full); 4 'Read-back' (nurse repeats); 5 'Owner' (who acts, when called back); 6 'Record' (chart, time). Icon of a phone at start, a clock at the end labeled '2 a.m.'

card: A pediatric nephrologist and a dialysis nurse talking at a dialysis chair where a young boy sits with his mother, warm light, no text.
